lstm_seed10_marker_count_only_check.hypothesis: lstm seed10 uses marker_count alone, with no positional/parity/balance refinement.
lstm_seed10_marker_count_only_check.interpretation: Three independent counterfactual types (marker_position, length_parity, balance) all show near-zero behavioral gap for lstm seed10, while marker_count alone shows a large gap (8.59) -- convergent null evidence across every structural refinement tested, plus one clear positive. A fourth, content-varying counterfactual (marker preserved at count=1 and centered, only mirror CONTENT varied) would complete the picture by ruling out content-sensitivity too -- this is exactly what balanced_content_match (condition 3, about to run) tests for EVERY architecture, so seed10's result there will serve as this confirmation without needing a redundant fifth counterfactual built here. Working attribution: marker_count-only, pending condition 3's content-null confirmation.

notable_findings_for_user: transformer seed1 ALSO shows length-parity-SPECIFIC sensitivity (length_parity_pairs gap=0.88, balance_pairs gap=0.04, ruled out by elimination) -- weaker in magnitude than rnn (8.2-8.6) but the same qualitative mechanism. This refines the corrected P4 narrative: length-parity sensitivity is NOT rnn-exclusive. transformer seed9 shows no such effect (length_parity_pairs gap=0.047, right at the threshold, essentially null) -- so this is a SEED-level split within transformer too, not just within lstm.

mamba (both seeds) and lstm seed1 all show DIRECT is_balanced/marker-centering sensitivity (balance_pairs gap 5.2-8.3), not just raw marker_position-bin sensitivity -- i.e. these architectures are sensitive to fine-grained (1-position) marker shifts, not only the coarse near/far distinction marker_position_pairs tested. This is a MORE refined mechanism than the P4 corrected summary's "marker_count/marker_position, no length-parity refinement" description implied -- "no length-parity refinement" remains true for these cells, but they are not using the crudest possible marker check either.

lstm shows THREE distinct mechanisms across its two probed seeds: seed10 = marker_count only (simplest in the pilot); seed1 = marker_count + marker_position + is_balanced (most refined non-rnn mechanism, comparable in sophistication to mamba). This is the most extreme seed-dependent mechanism split found in either pilot task.
